title: Metformin ameliorates doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity targeting HMGB1/TLR4/NLRP3 signaling pathway in mice.
authors: Alzokaky, Amany A; Al-Karmalawy, Ahmed A; Saleh, Mohamed A; Abdo, Walied; Farage, Amira E; Belal, Amany; Abourehab, Mohammed A S; Antar, Samar A
one_liner_zh: 该文研究二甲双胍对阿霉素心脏毒性的保护作用，聚焦HMGB1/TLR4/NLRP3炎症通路，仅含少量分子对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: AIMS: Oxidative stress and inflammation have been linked to doxorubicin (DOX)-induced cardiotoxicity, while the exact molecular processes are currently under investigation. The goal of this study is to investigate Metformin's preventive role in cardiotoxicity induced by DOX. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Male albino mice were divided randomly into 4 groups. Metformin (Met) 200 mg/kg orally (p.o.) was given either alone or when combined with a single DOX (15 mg/kg; i.p.). A control group of 5 mice was also provided. Met was initiated 7 days before DOX, lasting for 14 days. Besides, docking studies of Met towards HMGB1, NF-kB, and caspase 3 were performed. KEY FINDINGS: Heart weight, cardiac troponin T (cTnT), creatine kinase Myocardial Band (CK-MB) levels, malondialdehyde (MDA), and nitric oxide (NO) contents all increased significantly when comparing the DOX group to the control normal group. Conversely, there was a substantial decline in superoxide dismutase (SOD) and glutathione peroxidase (GSH). DOX group depicts a high expression of TLR4, HMGB1, and caspase 3. Immunohistochemical staining revealed an increase in NLRP3 inflammasome and NF-kappaB expressions alongside histopathological modifications. Additionally, Met dramatically decreased cardiac weight, CK-MB, and cTnT while maintaining the tissues' histological integrity. Inflammatory biomarkers, including HMGB1, TLR4, NF-kappaB, inflammasome, and caspase 3 were reduced after Met therapy. Furthermore, molecular docking studies suggested the antagonistic activity of Met towards HMGB1, NF-kappaB, and caspase 3 target receptors. SIGNIFICANCE: According to recent evidence, Met is a desirable strategy for improving cardiac toxicity produced by DOX by inhibiting the HMGB1/NF-kappaB inflammatory pathway, thus preserving heart function.
abstract_zh: 目的：氧化应激和炎症已被认为与多柔比星（DOX）诱导的心脏毒性相关，而确切的分子机制目前仍在研究中。本研究旨在探讨二甲双胍（Metformin）对DOX所致心脏毒性的预防作用。材料与方法：雄性白化小鼠随机分为4组。单独给予二甲双胍（Met）200 mg/kg口服（p.o.），或与单次DOX（15 mg/kg；腹腔注射i.p.）联合使用。另设5只小鼠作为对照组。Met在DOX给药前7天开始，持续14天。此外，还对Met与HMGB1、NF-kB和caspase 3进行了分子对接研究。主要发现：与正常对照组相比，DOX组的心脏重量、心肌肌钙蛋白T（cTnT）、肌酸激酶心肌带（CK-MB）水平、丙二醛（MDA）和一氧化氮（NO）含量均显著增加。相反，超氧化物歧化酶（SOD）和谷胱甘肽过氧化物酶（GSH）则显著下降。DOX组显示TLR4、HMGB1和caspase 3的高表达。免疫组织化学染色显示NLRP3炎症小体和NF-kappaB表达增加，同时伴有组织病理学改变。此外，Met显著降低了心脏重量、CK-MB和cTnT，同时维持了组织的组织学完整性。炎症生物标志物，包括HMGB1、TLR4、NF-kappaB、炎症小体和caspase 3，在Met治疗后均有所降低。此外，分子对接研究提示Met对HMGB1、NF-kappaB和caspase 3靶受体具有拮抗活性。意义：根据最新证据，Met通过抑制HMGB1/NF-kappaB炎症通路，从而保护心脏功能，是改善DOX所致心脏毒性的理想策略。
